svg.aria-label: Grading the Graders: Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Spark Open compared on 179 frozen SEC filings
svg.text: ATLAS-7 FILING SENTINEL · OPEN MODEL GRADING

text.font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', 'Liberation Serif', 'DejaVu Serif', serif

svg.text: Two Meta models took the same exam: 179 real SEC filings, frozen before either model saw them, scored against a locked answer key.
Corpus scope: 38 complete submissions, 141 primary-plus-EX-99. Temperature 0. Any verdict below 0.85 confidence had to be sat out.
THE MIRROR: THE TWO MODELS AGAINST EACH OTHER

text.font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', 'Liberation Serif', 'DejaVu Serif', serif

svg.text: the same verdict on 173 of 179 filings
They found the same 12 real signals, and missed the same 8.
They were wrong together on 21 filings.
They parted on only 6 filings, and all 6 were false alarms
on routine paper: 5 raised by the open model, 1 by the served.
SIDE BY SIDE: THE TWO MODELS, METRIC BY METRIC
each row on its own scale; the line between the dots is the gap

180 calls, none failed · 1,231,707 tokens · $2.34 the run
Abstentions: 0 on either run. The lowest verdict
probability anywhere was 0.88, above the 0.85 band.
Both gold-ABSTAIN filings were graded anyway, at 0.90+.
An empty, filing-shaped document, graded by both.
Both returned NO SIGNAL at probability 1.00,
One case, both models: Cloudflare’s Form 144, gold SIGNAL, clustered insider sales. Reading the document alone, both called it routine paper.
